claim: In adversarial training, resistance to attack is learned mainly from correctly classified training images that sit well away from the decision boundary, not from those hugging it. Call an image near-boundary if it can still be flipped at a tenth of the full perturbation budget, and far otherwise. Weakening the perturbation applied to near-boundary images should cost much less robustness than weakening it for far images. Supported only if, for weakening to a tenth of the budget and to zero, the robustness lost is smaller for near-boundary images than for far ones in both cases, full-strength perturbation of the far images beats both weakened variants on robust accuracy, and at least one way of drawing that near/far line raises clean and robust accuracy together relative to treating all correctly classified images the same.

experiments: Does the training signal for robustness come from images near the decision boundary? Setup: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, 100 epochs of standard PGD adversarial training at a perturbation budget of 8/255, with currently misclassified images fed in clean. Mark as near-boundary any correctly classified natural image that can still be flipped at one tenth of the budget (0.8/255). Train variants that cut the perturbation on those near-boundary images to the tenth, or to zero. Measured: clean and robust accuracy. Result: cutting perturbation on near-boundary images barely moves robustness, and the intermediate setting improves clean accuracy over perturbing them fully. Caveat: the comparison is only shown as a figure; the text gives no numbers.

The matching test on images far from the boundary. Setup: same CIFAR-10 / ResNet-18 run, but now cut the perturbation to the tenth or to zero for correctly classified images that survive attack at that reduced radius. Measured: clean and robust accuracy. Result: unlike the near-boundary case, robustness drops substantially; learning it needs these images perturbed at the full budget. Direction only, again figure-based with no numbers in the text.

Does the rule used to split near from far matter to both objectives? Setup: same training setup, alternative splitting rules. Measured: clean and robust accuracy. Result: the split changes both, and a suitable one improves both together. The text neither lists the rules compared nor gives their numbers.
